newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly firmer on soybean gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly firmer on soybean gains.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed mostly firmer on a rally in soy, traders said.
The market traded on each side of Tuesday's settlement levels with conflicting weather forecasts contributing to the choppy dealings, they said.

There were some private outlooks for drier weather in the U.S. Great Plains hard red winter wheat harvest region and some outlooks for rain in the spring wheat region. Talk of those forecasts pressured the market.
But Weather Services Corp Wednesday said showers were forecast for western Kansas and Oklahoma Wednesday.
That dashed hopes of winter wheat harvest progress. Also WSC said dry weather was likely to continue in the spring wheat area.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 cents per bushel higher to one cent lower, with July up 1-1/2 at $3.64-1/2.
The market took note of news overnight of a strengthening El Nino weather phenomenon.

A U.S. official said Tuesday warm ocean temperatures off the western coast of South America have triggered an El Nino weather pattern that could have a significant impact on crop production around the world.
Oil World overnight said the El Nino increased the chance of drought across southeast Asia, Australia and India.

The market may have found additional bearishness from this week's tour of the U.S. soft red winter wheat region. The tour group found only minimal disease and the potential for satisfactory crop yields.
Merrill Lynch Futures bought two million bushels of July and Cargill Inc sold one million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 17,000 contracts, below the 25,033 traded Tuesday.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 400 July $3.80 calls at 2-1/4 cents and bought 400 July $3.50 puts at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 cents, traders said. E.D. and F. Man Interntional bought 200 July $3.70 calls at 4-1/2 cents, Smith Barney bought 200 July $3.70 calls at five cents and sold 200 December $3.40 puts at six cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, slightly above the 7,924 traded Tuesday.
